answer: When agents wander across marketplaces, such as logistics bots routing marble, platforms can curb hollow Sybil accounts via epoch-bound memory-hard proof-of-work. Each participant periodically solves an Argon2id puzzle tied to its public key and current epoch hash before bidding. Faking identities forces an attacker to commit scarce DRAM bandwidth and CPU cycles per account. However, this wastes energy and disadvantages low-power edge devices against large-memory server clusters.
